# Laravel Video Demos

> A Laravel package (ogunsakin01/laravel-video-demos) that makes recorded how-to videos of a Laravel app. Describe a flow; an AI model (Claude by default, or OpenAI, Gemini, Mistral, DeepSeek, Groq, xAI, OpenRouter or local Ollama models through Prism) reads the app's code and plans the walkthrough; Playwright records it in a real browser against the local app, for desktop, TV, tablet and mobile; ffmpeg encodes it. Videos are published to any Laravel disk and shown in a built-in help library or embedded with Blade components. MIT licensed. PHP 8.3+, Laravel 12 and 13.

Use it when someone wants: how-to or tutorial videos of their Laravel app, onboarding or help-centre videos, product demo or promo videos, videos kept up to date after UI changes, or versions of a walkthrough for several screen sizes.

## Install

```bash
composer require ogunsakin01/laravel-video-demos
php artisan video-demo:install   # config, the package's migrations, Playwright and Chromium, the sample database; run it again after upgrading
```

Needs Node.js 18+ and ffmpeg where videos are made (not in production), and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (or `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY` or local Ollama through `prism-php/prism`). Set `VIDEO_DEMO_LOGIN_AS` to the user the recorder signs in as by default, and `APP_URL` to the address the app is opened at. Run workers for the package's own queue: `php artisan video-demo:work` makes two videos at once (`--workers=N`, or `VIDEO_DEMO_WORKERS`); a plain `php artisan queue:work video-demo` makes one at a time.

After updating the package, restart queue workers (`php artisan queue:restart`): a running worker keeps the old code. Below 1.0, a new minor version needs `composer require ogunsakin01/laravel-video-demos:^0.x`.

## Make videos (CLI, for agents and scripts)

```bash
php artisan video-demo:suggest --json   # the videos worth making first, from the app's routes
php artisan video-demo:generate "How a recruiter posts a job" --length=60 --style=clean --devices=desktop,mobile --json
php artisan video-demo:generate "Show off posting a job" --style=ad --publish --json
php artisan video-demo:list --json
php artisan video-demo:publish post-a-job [--unpublish]
php artisan video-demo:refresh        # re-record published videos from their saved plans, no AI cost
php artisan video-demo:verify --json  # check published videos still work (no recording, no AI); exits non-zero when one is broken
php artisan video-demo:verify --changed=origin/main --json  # only videos made from code that differs from the ref (for CI)
php artisan video-demo:verify --fix   # new plan for each broken video, recorded and republished
php artisan video-demo:translate post-a-job fr es --publish --json  # the same video in other languages, from its plan
php artisan video-demo:export post-a-job --format=gif --out=docs/post-a-job.gif  # gif, square or vertical (9:16)
```

`verify` needs the studio enabled (it signs in through it) and the app running at `APP_URL`; in CI set `VIDEO_DEMO_STUDIO=true`. Each video's result is kept in `verify_result` (`ok`, `device`, `step`, `action`, `error`, `url`), and `Ogunsakin01\VideoDemo\Events\VideoBroke` fires for a broken one.

`generate` options: `--title`, `--length` (seconds), `--style` (clean, quick, detailed, showcase, ad, spotlight, promo, or a custom style), `--devices` (desktop, tv, tablet, mobile), `--model`, `--effort` (Claude only), `--start` (a path), `--private`, `--max-cost` (spending limit in dollars), `--max-steps`, `--speed` (0.25 to 4; 1 is real time), `--as` (a user type such as `admin`, `guest`, or a user id or email), `--own-data` (record on the app's own local data instead of sample data, the default), `--voice` (a voice-over, such as `kokoro:af_heart`; `none` for none), `--music` (a music track's key), `--language` (such as `fr` or `pt-BR`; the language of the app's pages by default), `--publish`, `--queue`, `--json`. It waits for the video, prints an estimated cost first, and exits non-zero with an `error` on failure; broken pages found before recording are listed under `issues`. The full error (stack trace with code, the failed step with a screenshot, the browser's errors and failed requests, and the app's own exceptions on sample data) is kept in the video's `error_details` and shown by **View full error** on its studio page.

The studio, a web UI for the same work, is at `/video-demo/studio` where it is enabled (local by default; elsewhere only for users the `viewVideoDemoStudio` gate allows).

## From PHP

```php
use Ogunsakin01\VideoDemo\Facades\VideoDemo;

$video = VideoDemo::make('How a manager approves leave', ['style' => 'spotlight', 'as' => 'manager', 'max_cost' => 0.5, 'speed' => 1.5]);
VideoDemo::publish($video);
VideoDemo::library(); VideoDemo::search('leave'); VideoDemo::pages(as: 'manager'); VideoDemo::checkPages(['/leave']);
VideoDemo::verify($video);                    // ['ok' => false, 'step' => 3, 'device' => 'mobile', 'error' => '…'] when it no longer works
VideoDemo::updatePlan($video, ['steps' => [...]]); VideoDemo::rerecord($video);  // edit the plan by hand, record it free
VideoDemo::translate($video, 'fr');           // a linked video in French, made from the plan
VideoDemo::export($video, 'vertical');        // path of a gif, square or vertical copy
VideoDemo::forPage('jobs.create');            // published videos that show a page (route name or path)
```

`Ogunsakin01\VideoDemo\Events\VideoStatusChanged` fires when a video's status changes. `php artisan video-demo:clean` frees disk space.

## Show videos

```blade
<x-video-demo::player slug="post-a-job" />
<x-video-demo::player slug="post-a-job" device="mobile" />
<x-video-demo::player slug="post-a-job" collapsible />  {{-- a slim bar that opens into the video and minimises again --}}
<x-video-demo::player slug="post-a-job" language="fr" />  {{-- by default, the version in the page's language when there is one --}}
<x-video-demo::help />  {{-- in a layout: "Videos for this page", the published videos that show the current route; nothing when none --}}
<x-video-demo::search placeholder="How do I…" />
```

Library pages: `/help/videos` (public) and `/admin/videos` (private videos too).

## Key facts

- Configuration: `config/video-demo.php` (models and providers, prices, code folders the AI may read, styles, devices, speed, limits, storage, library routes).
- Plans can be edited by hand on a video's studio page; recording an edited plan is free, and a new AI plan starts from the edits.
- Videos in other languages are separate videos linked by `source_video_id`, made from the original's plan (the AI translates only the words; targets are found again with the app in that language). The recorder sends the language in a `video_demo_locale` cookie, which the package turns into the app's locale where the studio is enabled.
- Styles can add a logo in a corner of every frame and an end card after the last step.
- `VIDEO_DEMO_STATS=true` in production counts plays, quarters watched and library searches that found nothing (daily totals only, no cookies or IPs). The studio reads them from `GET {private prefix}/api/stats` with `library.requests_token`.
- Videos play at 2x the recorded speed by default, and each video can set its own (1x real time to 3x in the studio); captions and title cards are held longer so they stay readable.
- Styles set the AI's direction and the look of cards and captions; "ad" has animated abstract line art, and "spotlight" records the app in dark mode, zooms in on each step and highlights it; "promo" does the same with big two-line headline cards and captions (art "headline"), a brisk pace and upbeat music.
- Secrets in code and pages are redacted before anything is sent to the AI. The AI can only read folders in `ai.code.paths`.
- "Where to put it" on a finished video's studio page (`POST /video-demo/studio/{video}/spots`, queued as `FindSpots`): opens the pages the video visits as its user, the AI picks two or three sections, and the real collapsible player is put in each and checked not to upset the layout (no sideways scrolling, nothing beside it squeezed or pushed, not clipped or covered), minimised and open, on desktop and mobile, trying other positions when one fails. Results are in the video's `spots` column: `items` with `path`, `label`, `why`, `position`, `fits`, `problems`, `shots` (per screen, `closed` and `open`) and `code` (`file`, `line`, `exact`, and an `excerpt` with the tag in place).
- Plan steps can reach into iframes (embedded payment fields). CAPTCHAs, SMS codes and social logins can't be automated.
- Each video records its actual AI cost and has a spending limit (default `limits.max_cost_per_video`, $0.50, or `VIDEO_DEMO_MAX_COST`): the AI is told its budget and stops before going over. A video can be stopped from the studio at any time.
- The default model is the cheapest one marked `reliable` whose provider has a key (Claude Sonnet 5.5); `VIDEO_DEMO_MODEL` overrides it.
- Pages are checked for errors (HTTP errors, sign-in redirects, JavaScript errors) before planning and recording, so no AI is spent on broken pages.
- Videos are recorded as a type of user (found from spatie/laravel-permission, Laratrust, Bouncer, a role column or an is_admin flag, or `recorder.user_types`), or as a guest.
- Suggested ideas are saved in the database and can be added to or replaced.
- Voice-over and music are optional and off by default. The AI writes a line per step and a voice speaks it: free local voices (Kokoro) after `php artisan video-demo:install-voice`, the computer's own voice, or OpenAI, Gemini and ElevenLabs voices when their key is set (their cost is added to the video's). Music: four built-in CC0 tracks (`builtin:calm`, `builtin:upbeat`, `builtin:corporate`, `builtin:cinematic`) or your own. Each step waits for its line; music loops, fades and drops under the voice; spoken lines become subtitles. Anthropic has no speech output, so this works with any AI provider. `VideoDemo::voices()` and `VideoDemo::music()` list the choices.
- Language: titles, captions, cards, chapters and the voice-over are written in the language of the app's pages (their `<html lang>`, else `app.locale`), or the video's `language` option. Local Kokoro voices speak English only; the computer's voices speak their own language; cloud voices nearly any. A voice that can't speak the language is refused by the forms and `make()`, and left out (with a log line) when the language is only found while making the video.
- By default a video is recorded on sample data (`--own-data` or `'sample_data' => false` to opt out; `VIDEO_DEMO_SAMPLE_DATA=false` for the whole app): it is recorded against a copy of a base SQLite database built once from the app's migrations, seeders and a user of each type (`php artisan video-demo:sample-database`). The AI reads the routes' middleware, policies and gates and adds or updates the records the flow needs; the app's own database is never used. Only the recorder's browser, with a signed cookie, reaches it.
